subject: general
question: A bus travelling at 14 km/hr completes a journey in 20 hours. What should its speed be to cover the same distance in 5 hours?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time.

Time ratio = 20 : 5 = 4 : 1

Speed ratio = 1 : 4

Initial speed (1 ratio part) = 14 km/hr

New speed (4 ratio parts) = 14 × 4 = 56 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 56 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Speed (S₁) = 14 km/hr

Initial Time (T₁) = 20 hours

New Time (T₂) = 5 hours

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

 
 
 
• 
 Constant Distance
 
• 
 

 Speed = 14 km/hr | Time = 20 hours
 
• 
 

 Speed = ? km/hr | Time = 5 hours

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = S₁ × T₁

⇒ Total Distance = 14 × 20 = 280 km

⇒ To cover the same distance in 5 hours, the new speed (S₂) is required.

⇒ S₂ = Distance ÷ T₂

⇒ S₂ = 280 ÷ 5 = 56 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 56 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Proportionality of Speed and Time

When the distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to the time taken (S ∝ 1/T).

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If equal distances are covered at different speeds x and y, Average Speed = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Unit Conversion Trick

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.
